A quick reference to every tool and data source this book uses, gathered in one place.

## Where to Find Data

- **[Delaware Open Data Portal](https://data.delaware.gov/)** — real government
  datasets (traffic crashes, school enrollment, park locations, COVID-19
  trends, and more). Used throughout this book, starting in Chapter 2.
- **[Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets)** — a huge library of datasets and
  a learning community, mentioned as an alternative data source starting in
  Chapter 2.

## Tools Used in This Book

- **[CODAP](https://codap.concord.org/)** — free, no-login drag-and-drop data
  visualization, used in Chapter 3. See also CODAP's official
  [How-to Guides](https://codap.concord.org/help/how-to-guides/).
- **Google Sheets** — spreadsheet formulas, filtering, and pivot tables, used
  in Chapter 2.
- **PyCharm** — a Python IDE, set up in Chapter 4 (see also
  [Getting Set Up](getting-set-up.qmd)).
- **[Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com)** — a no-install
  alternative to PyCharm, covered in [Getting Set Up](getting-set-up.qmd).
- **[Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com)** — a genuinely free weather API
  (no account, no API key), used in Chapter 6 to teach how APIs work. See its
  [documentation](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs) for the full range of
  endpoints. Chapter 6 also points curious readers to the
  [Open Notify ISS position API](http://api.open-notify.org/iss-now.json) as
  a second free, no-key API to try.
- **[scikit-learn](https://scikit-learn.org/)** — the machine learning
  library used in Chapter 8.
